declared.scope: Freezes the shared evaluation method and the exact runner recipe for every deliverable-2 row that is prepared for measurement (controlled + system_comparison rows listed in prepared_comparisons). It produces no baseline number; deliverable 4 runs the recipes and reads the reports. A recipe measures the system its runtime binding names (see each recipe's head source), not 'the checkpoint' in the abstract.
out_of_scope: per-detector threshold re-tuning variants (the matched-baseline study's cs/cst/ntt fair points): a separate declaration with its own pairs, never merged with fixed-policy rows

--double-buffer headline throughput (config D of the reproducibility study): a separate execution profile that must be declared before use; numbers under it are not comparable to this contract's serial profile
A1/A2 raw pretrained-YOLO rows (no runner in the inventory)
historical results (no preset/engine sha, no runtime identity; never reusable as a paired side)
training-cache rebuilds and any new training arm (a rebuilt cache is a new node, not the old one)

dataset.note: Every s/m checkpoint in the lineage was trained on these seven sequences (inventory dataset_split.train); this contract is therefore an in-domain measurement and says so. Frame range is always the full sequence (max_frames unset); a run that passes --max-frames is refused.

evaluator.clear_and_idf1: motmetrics (version recorded in the run identity). gt loaded with fmt=mot15-2D min_confidence=1 (only 'consider' rows), predictions with min_confidence=-1 (nothing dropped), IoU distance with distth 0.5, accumulated per sequence; the overall numbers are ratios over the summed idtp/idfp/idfn/FP/FN/IDs/objects counts (src/saccade/perception/eval/metrics.py). No distractor-class filtering on this path.
evaluator.hota: HOTA/DetA/AssA via the vendored third_party/TrackEval (git tree recorded in the run identity; SACCADE_TRACKEVAL_ROOT must be unset) with TrackEval's MotChallenge2DBox preprocessing (distractor / zero-marked removal). The evaluator prints and skips HOTA when TrackEval is unimportable; the runner marks such a run incomplete.
evaluator.output_layer: The MOT file is the tracker's own output including its configured post-processing (interpolate_tracklets etc. from the resolved config); those keys are tracker policy, not evaluator settings, and are pinned by the resolved config sha.
evaluator.precision_of_record: Metrics are recorded as the evaluator prints them (one decimal, percent). Deltas smaller than the print precision are not resolvable under this contract; deliverable 4 must not manufacture extra digits.

timing.clock: host wall-clock (time.perf_counter) inside the evaluator; a frame is complete when its tracker output rows are on the host (track_results_on_host) and appended to the sequence result
timing.start_point: top of _run_frame, before the frame is fetched from the streamer (t_e2e_start); under the serial profile the fetch waits for the streamer's background GPU decode (prefetch depth 2), so decode time counts only insofar as it is not hidden by that prefetch
timing.end_point: _record_frame_timing at output emission of the same frame; under the serial profile no frame is deferred, so there is no double-buffer final drain
timing.decode_included: partially (see start_point): JPEG decode runs on a background thread ahead of the frame; the measured interval includes the wait for it, not its full cost
timing.warmup: the first warmup_frames (resolved config, 50) frames of every sequence are excluded from latency and throughput
timing.throughput: per sequence: frames after warmup / (last frame completion - first measured frame start); overall: sum of frames / sum of per-sequence intervals (the 'Overall throughput' line and _fps_summary.txt); model load, CUDA-graph capture, sequence setup, result-file write and metric scoring are outside every interval
timing.artifacts: _latency_profile_<seq>.json (mean/p95/p99/samples), _latency_profile.json, _fps_summary.txt in the run dir; the runner copies the summaries (minus samples) into contract_run.json
timing.comparability: latency/throughput are comparable only between runs of the same execution profile on the same environment identity; the eager profile's FPS is a lower bound (no compile, no graphs) and never a deployment number

whole_graph_serial.description: the family preset as declared: TRT backbone engine + whole-detect CUDA graph + tracker graph + graphed main NMS, torch.compile on (preset default), GPU JPEG decode (preset default), serial scheduling (no --double-buffer), single process (processes 0, cpp_threads 0)
whole_graph_serial.temporal_blocks: whole-graph forward is single-frame: a temporal checkpoint's blocks are bypassed, effective T=1 (build_mamba_gated_detector)
whole_graph_serial.head_source: the preset's mamba_head_engine when named (m preset) unless the recipe carries --no-mamba-trt; see each recipe's head source

eager_pytorch.description: mamba_pyt_backbone preset: PyTorch backbone taken from --mamba-teacher-ckpt (fpn_backbone_engine empty), no whole-graph / cuda / tracker graph, --no-compile (eager), GPU JPEG decode, serial, single process; the tracker policy is brought to the production s preset by explicit overrides (section 6)
eager_pytorch.temporal_blocks: a temporal Mamba checkpoint would run the STREAMING temporal path by default on this profile; every eager Mamba recipe carries --no-temporal so the effective forward is T=1, matching the whole-graph rows
eager_pytorch.head_source: the endpoint's own checkpoint head: TeacherHeadDetector (native Detect head, gate-free) for gated_teacher_ckpt nodes; the Mamba head in PyTorch for mamba_ckpt nodes (--no-mamba-trt); the eager preset's default mamba_ckpt is cleared with --mamba-ckpt '' on native-head rows because mot17.py refuses both

tracker_policy.rule: One fixed tracker policy per execution profile. Whole-graph rows use their family preset as declared (s and m presets differ in kalman_r_scale and the relink bridge gate; that difference is part of the E1 system difference and is frozen as such). Eager rows all use the production s tracker policy: the eager preset is brought to it by CLI overrides derived at freeze time (every resolved key that differs between source_preset and eager_preset outside the execution/artifact keys).
tracker_policy.declared_limit: E3 (m native head vs m Mamba head) therefore runs under the s production tracker policy, not m's retuned policy (kalman_r_scale 3.5, relaxed bridge gate). This is a fixed-policy comparison by declaration; an m-policy variant would be a separate pair id.
tracker_policy.per_detector_retuning: forbidden inside a pair: both sides run the identical resolved tracker keys (validate-pair refuses any config difference outside the treatment)

runtime_env.why: the evaluator reads escape hatches from the environment (SACCADE_FRESHNESS_W, SACCADE_STABILITY_W, SACCADE_ENABLE_DDA, SACCADE_DDA_MAX_COST, SACCADE_GMC_PCR_THRESH, SACCADE_GPU_RELINK_GATE, SACCADE_STREAM_MODE, SACCADE_DOUBLE_BUFFER, SACCADE_DETECT_BARRIER, SACCADE_MAIN_NMS_GRAPHED, ...) that the resolved config cannot see; the runner refuses to start when any non-allowed SACCADE_* variable is set, rather than recording it
runtime_env.child_env: SACCADE_BUILD_PATH = the resolved native build dir (its *.so digests are part of the environment identity); LD_LIBRARY_PATH gets torch/lib prepended (the cuBLAS resolution the eval drivers use); the parent-run claim variables let mot17.py join the runner's manifest instead of publishing its own
runtime_env.cwd: the checkout root (every artifact path is relative to it)

identity.bound_where: run_manifest.json schema v3, field runtime_identity, written by open_run before mot17.py starts (production provenance mode); mot17.py joins that claim via SACCADE_PARENT_RUN_ROOT/CLAIM
pairing_keys: resolved_config_sha256 (every argparse dest after preset merge + argv, minus run_local_keys)

artifacts.<key>.sha256 for every non-empty artifact dest (mamba_ckpt, mamba_teacher_ckpt, mamba_yolo_weights, fpn_backbone_engine, mamba_head_engine, teacher_head_ckpt, teacher_head_backbone_engine, engine)
environment (hostname, platform, python, torch/torchvision/tensorrt/numpy/motmetrics versions, GPU name, driver, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, build dir + native *.so digests, TrackEval git tree + dirty)
dirty (always false for repeat/formal; bound so a smoke identity never collides with a clean one)
identity.identity_sha256: sha256 of the pairing block; repeat reports and formal runs are matched on it
identity.fail_closed: missing manifest, reconstructed provenance, missing/foreign runtime_identity schema, contract sha mismatch, incomplete run record, non-formal stage, or any identity path differing outside the pair's allowed_differences => not_paired

smoke.purpose: prove the recipe executes end to end (model load, graph capture, every required metric key incl. HOTA) on the smoke sequence set
smoke.status: procedure evidence only; a sequence-subset run; may run on a dirty tree; never pairable, never a baseline

repeat.purpose: observe run-to-run variance of one identity on the full sequence set before any formal number exists
repeat.identity_rule: all runs of a report share one identity_sha256 (which binds commit and dirty; repeat runs require a clean tree, so a report produced on edited sources can never unlock a formal run at the same HEAD); byte identity via scripts/tools/eval_repeat_identity.py (raw MOT identity incl. track ids) and the observed metric range per key; only repeat-stage runs enter a report
repeat.claim_rule: report 'k distinct outputs in n runs' and the observed range; never 'deterministic' / 'bit-exact'; zero divergences in n runs only rule out per-run divergence rates above ~1-0.05^(1/n) (n=3: ~63%, n=6: ~39%) at 95% one-sided, so min_runs is a floor for procedure, not evidence of reproducibility (docs/research/eval/nogpudecode_reproducibility_20260907.md)
repeat.reproducibility_is_per_configuration: no recipe inherits another recipe's repeat evidence; a treatment arm does not inherit its base arm's

formal.note: a formal run is refused unless a complete repeat report with >= repeat.min_runs runs exists for the same identity_sha256 under the recipe's run root; a formal run is not a baseline by itself — baseline status is assigned in deliverable 4 against the repeat report's observed range

procedure.single_run_rule: no run, formal or otherwise, is a determinism claim; a single-run delta below the same-identity observed range reads as 'not distinguishable from run-to-run variation', and a delta above it does not automatically prove an effect

variance_axes.runtime_repeat: same identity, repeated runs (repeat reports): what the measurement instrument resolves
variance_axes.training_seed: seed_replicate pairs (D1-D4): different checkpoints from the same recipe at different seeds; a training-process quantity
variance_axes.rule: never pooled and never substituted: a treatment delta is read against runtime_repeat for resolvability and against training_seed for attributability; a seed-replicate delta is not a runtime-repeat estimate and vice versa
